title: Rails Security
intro: Rails ships with security protections on by default — CSRF via protect_from_forgery, XSS via ERB auto-escaping, SQL injection prevention via parameterised queries in where clauses, mass assignment protection via strong parameters, and clickjacking prevention via X-Frame-Options. The interview question is not 'what does Rails protect you from?' but 'how do engineers accidentally turn those protections off?' — and that is a much harder question. This page covers each Rails default and its bypass: html_safe and raw for XSS, string interpolation in where for SQLi, missing permit for mass assignment, skipping the CSRF token for API endpoints. It also covers the OWASP Top 10 mapped to Rails, Content-Security-Policy headers, and secure cookie flags.
